To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the evolution of the accretion disk is strongly influenced by the energy dissipation in the coronal region, and (ii) the disk can evolve into a state in which it exhibits coherent oscillations with amplitudes that are consistent with the QPOs observed recently in the low state of the Rapid Burster.

the evolution of accretions disks with coronae can explain: 1) the observed quasi-periodic oscillatory behavior of the X-ray flux in the Rapid Bursters, 2) the observed QPOs in the black hole candidates, and 3) the observed spectral differences between the high and low state of the black hole candidates.

the low frequency QPOs observed from X-ray binary systems can be explained in the context of a model in which the mass accretions and angular momentum transport occur in a viscous accretion disk and the gravitational energy released is dissipated both in an optically thin corona and in an optically thicker disk.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the global nonlinear time dependent behavior of accretion flow systems.
a new class of accretion models in which the disk-corona system plays a crucial role in regulating the mass flow in the system.
the evolution of accretions disks with coronae and the implications for the QPOs in black hole candidate sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the low frequency QPOs observed are the result of the nonlinear time-dependent evolution of accretions disk-corona systems.
the QPOs observed are a consequence of the global nonlinear time dependent behavior of accretion flow in the inner regions of X-ray binary systems.
the observed QPOs in the low frequency range are due to the thermal-viscous instabilities in the inner region of the optically thick disk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of the accretion flow in black hole candidate systems can be described by a single model, and that the observed QPOs in the high state are a result of the disk instabilities.
the low frequency QPOs are a global phenomenon in accretion disks.
the low frequency QPOs observed recently in MXB 1735-335 and some black hole candidates are likely due to the global oscillations of an optically thick accretion disk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of an optically thin corona is a necessary condition for generating coherent oscillations in the disk.
a corona can effectively reduce the amplitude of the mass flow oscillations generated from the thermal or viscous instabilities, and can also reduce the amplitude of QPOs.
a corona can play a significant role in the evolution of an accretion disk, and that a corona could be a possible mechanism to explain the observed QPOs.
